We continue the bucket-model discussion, then use energy budgets to build a simple climate model with a surface and an atmospheric layer.

## Open the notebooks on LEAP

1. Download both `.ipynb` files using the links above.
2. Log in to [LEAP JupyterHub](https://leap.2i2c.cloud/) and start your server.
3. In JupyterLab, open your course repository folder and upload the notebooks using the file browser's upload button or drag and drop.
4. Open **Lab 1a** and select a Python kernel. Work through the cells in order with `Shift+Enter`.

Both notebooks need only NumPy and Matplotlib. The flux diagrams are embedded, so no separate data or image downloads are needed. For GitHub and submission help, see [Lab 0a](labs/lab0a.qmd).

## How we will work

Start with **Lab 1a** in pairs. Complete the cells marked **TODO**, test the equilibrium limits, explore atmospheric absorption, and check conservation of energy. The supplied checks will fail until the TODOs are completed; work cell by cell rather than choosing Run All at the start.

Then move to **Lab 1b**, which uses the same forward Euler method as the bucket model. Its integration and plotting code are supplied. Before running each experiment, write what you expect and why, then explain the results in your own words.

**Lab 1b, Section 5:** finish the changing-flux activity in class if time permits; otherwise complete it at home before submitting.

## Before submitting

- Complete the code and written responses in both notebooks.
- Restart the kernel and run each completed notebook from top to bottom. Check that the tests pass and the figures appear.
- Save the notebooks with their outputs in your private course GitHub repository, and commit and push your work.
- Submit your repository link on Courseworks following the existing course instructions. Check Courseworks for the deadline.
